stem: A tangent curve has an equation of the form $y=a\tan\theta+q$. Point $A$ is at $\left(0^{\circ}, {=q}\right)$ and point $B$ is at $\left(45^{\circ}, {=yb}\right)$; both points lie on the curve. Determine the values of $a$ and $q$.
solution: The constant $q$ shifts the graph up or down. For an unshifted tangent graph, point $A$ would be at $\left(0^{\circ}, 0\right)$. Here $A$ is at $\left(0^{\circ}, {=q}\right)$, so the graph has been shifted downwards by ${=abs(q)}$. Therefore $q={=q}$.
To find $a$, substitute $q={=q}$ and point $B$, $\left(45^{\circ}, {=yb}\right)$, into the equation. Remember that $\tan 45^{\circ}=1$.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Loses the sign of q
proposed_misconceptions.description: Reads the y-intercept (0 degrees, -3) as q = 3, or after substituting q = -3 subtracts 3 from y_B instead of adding 3, so that a and/or q carries the wrong sign.

notes: The book's typical exercise with the graph shifted DOWN (q a negative integer), second point at 45 degrees; y_B = a + q can be negative, zero or positive. Models ex6-8-34. NOTE: the book's printed solution of ex6-8-34 writes a(-1) for a tan 45 degrees (its answer a = 1 is nevertheless right because of a second sign slip); this family's steps use tan 45 = 1 throughout and do not reproduce that line. Figure not reproduced; both points are given as coordinates in the stem. a may be 1: the solution therefore does not print the complete equation, so it never reads 1tan.
